title: COVID-19, HIV, and Cryptococcal Meningitis Coinfections with Abnormal Laboratory Findings
case_prompt: A 28-year-old man was admitted with a seven-month history of malaise, fever, and headache, recently accompanied by increased cough and chest pain. His past history included hepatosplenomegaly, generalized lymphadenopathy, pleural effusion, hemoptysis, pancytopenia, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and plasma cell dyscrasia; he had discontinued therapy during prior hospitalizations. On admission to the infectious diseases ward, his mental status was normal and there were no skin or ocular lesions. Laboratory studies showed WBC 1.9×10^3 cells/mm^3, RBC 3.11×10^6 cells/mm^3, platelets 86×10^3 cells/mm^3, hemoglobin 6.2 g/dL, serum procalcitonin 0.068 ng/mL, and CRP 67.8 mg/L. A nasopharyngeal RT-PCR was positive for SARS-CoV-2 and chest CT demonstrated bilateral lung involvement; chest X-ray showed a right lobar pneumonia. Brain MRI revealed multiple hyperintense lesions in white matter. During the hospitalization, he developed dizziness, vomiting, sweating, and hyponatremia. An initial lumbar puncture revealed an elevated opening pressure, CSF WBC count 50 cells/mm^3 (70% neutrophils, 30% lymphocytes), glucose 35 mg/dL, protein 71 mg/dL, lactate dehydrogenase 64 mg/dL, adenosine deaminase 10.9 U/L, and CSF procalcitonin 0.084 ng/mL.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Metabolic disorders — “Metabolic diseases such as Wilson, poisoning with carbon monoxide, and drug reaction were in differential diagnostic list.”  
2. Bacterial meningitis — “Although rate of elevation in bacterial infections is more than viral and fungal disease, at least slight increase must be seen in critical fungal disease,” yet PCT remained normal.  
3. Cryptococcal antigen test — “Cryptococcal rapid antigen testing (Coris BioConcept, Belgium) of CSF was negative,” highlighting potential for false-negative results.
